questions.question: What two simultaneous design features let the proposed metasurface suppress pump radiation yet retain nonlinear THz emission?

options.A: Opposite-phase linear moments cancel while the second-order SRR responses add constructively
options.B: The dark mode suppresses both linear and nonlinear SRR currents
options.C: The two SRRs radiate linearly in phase but their nonlinear currents cancel
options.D: The silicon slab absorbs the THz output while transmitting the pump

questions.rationale: The paired SRRs are arranged for destructive interference of linear electric/magnetic moments, while their second-order responses have the same sign and radiate constructively.
questions.evidence_quote:
the nonlinear radiation of both SRRs adds
constructively in the far ﬁeld. The linear radiation, how-
ever, is opposite in phase and cancels in the far ﬁeld

questions.question: Which mode and structural element provide local-field enhancement in the designed emitter?

options.A: A TE2,0 dark mode of a thin silicon slab, quantized by metal walls
options.B: A bright TM1,0 mode of a thick gold film, quantized by SRR gaps
options.C: A Fabry–Perot mode in free space, selected by the detector aperture
options.D: A plasmonic dipole resonance in silicon nanorods without a slab

questions.rationale: The metal walls quantize slab modes, and the authors select the TE2,0 dark state to drive SRRs via evanescent surface fields.
questions.evidence_quote: we select the second quantized mode on the lowest branch of dispersion for the dielectric slab, that is, TE2,0 mode

questions.question: What symmetry/critical-coupling condition produces perfect absorption in the proposed sheet model?

options.A: Balanced electric and magnetic effective surface responses, with ζσs(e)=ζ−1σs(m)=2 ideally
options.B: Purely electric response with ζσs(e)=0 and magnetic response absent
options.C: Equal electric and magnetic conductivities of opposite sign and zero dissipative loss
options.D: A dark mode with zero coupling to both electric and magnetic pump fields

questions.rationale: Impedance matching balances electric and magnetic coupling; critical coupling then removes transmitted pump energy as well as reflection.
questions.evidence_quote:
Balancing the electric and magnetic
coupling allowed for impedance match, hence, eliminat-
ing the reﬂection of the pump energy. Tuning the cou-
pling strength to a critical case also allowed us to further
eliminate the linear transmitted ﬁeld

questions.question: At what SRR offsets did the authors identify the optimized near-perfect-absorption configuration, and what absorption did it reach?

options.A: Δx1≈70 nm and Δx2≈470 nm, with about 94% absorption
options.B: Δx1≈470 nm and Δx2≈70 nm, with about 49% absorption
options.D: Δx1≈50 nm and Δx2≈800 nm, with about 20% absorption

questions.rationale: The conductivities were scanned in 5-nm steps; the reported optimum is near those offsets with absorption as high as 94%.
questions.evidence_quote: the optimal case may be picked at ∆x1 ∼= 70 nm and ∆x2 ∼= 470 nm

questions.question: What geometric and excitation parameters were used for the FDTD estimate of nonlinear emission?

options.A: L=800 nm, W=240 nm, h=100 nm; a 140-fs pulse with peak field 2×107 V/m
options.B: L=240 nm, W=800 nm, h=50 nm; a 14-fs pulse with peak field 2×105 V/m
options.C: L=1.5 μm, W=100 nm, h=800 nm; a 140-ps pulse at 2×107 V/m
options.D: L=800 nm, W=50 nm, h=240 nm; a continuous wave at 2×109 V/m

questions.rationale: These dimensions set the dark-mode emitter and the simulations used a resonant Gaussian pulse with the specified duration and amplitude.
questions.evidence_quote: The geometric parameters of the unit are designed to have the length L = 800 nm, width W = 240 nm and thickness h = 100 nm

questions.question: Which part of the hydrodynamic electron-gas model is identified as crucial to second-order nonlinearity?

options.A: The convection term, contributing through products of current and accumulated surface charge
options.B: The linear Drude damping term, contributing through the square of the dielectric constant
options.C: The pressure term, contributing through a frequency-independent magnetic dipole
options.D: The diffusion term, contributing through a product of two incident fields only

questions.rationale: The authors describe the convection term as the source of second-order response, qualitatively involving current times charge density.
questions.evidence_quote: the convection term plays the crucial role for the second-order nonlinearities

questions.question: How large was the calculated THz-emission enhancement over the reference conventional SRR metasurface at optimized positions?

options.A: More than 120-fold in THz emission power
options.C: More than 120-fold in pump absorption only

questions.rationale: The performance map reports over 120-fold enhancement in THz emission power relative to the reference SRR configuration.
questions.evidence_quote: resulting in more than 120-fold enhancement in THz emission power

questions.question: What effective second-order susceptibility values are compared for the new design and conventional SRR metasurface?
questions.rationale: The calculated susceptibility is a little over one order of magnitude larger than that of the reference SRR.
questions.evidence_quote:
eﬀective nonlinear susceptibility of our designed meta-
surface χ(2)
dark ≈2.4 × 10−11 m/V, while that of the tradi-
tional SRR metasurface χ(2)
SRR ≈1.7 × 10−12 m/V

questions.question: What spectral characteristics of the generated THz signal follow from the pulse-envelope model in the paper?

options.A: A peak at ω=2/τ and FWHM bandwidth Δω≈2.31/τ
options.B: A peak at ω=1/τ and bandwidth Δω≈0.5/τ
options.C: A peak at the pump frequency ω0 and bandwidth set only by the SRR resonance
options.D: A flat spectrum extending to 4 THz, independent of pulse duration

questions.rationale: The emitted field is proportional to the second time derivative of the pulse envelope, yielding the stated peak and bandwidth scaling.
questions.evidence_quote: THz spectrum has the peak at ω = 2/τ with a bandwidth ∆ωFWHM ≈ 2.31/τ.

questions.question: What caveat limits interpretation of the paper's absolute THz conversion efficiency as an experimental prediction?

options.A: The simulations use a spatially infinite surface under plane-wave illumination, so the model is not suited to predict setup-specific absolute numbers
options.B: The nonlinear current was omitted from the FDTD calculations
options.C: The reference SRR data were unavailable for side-by-side comparison
options.D: The model assumes a substrate but experimental metasurfaces cannot use one

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly say their simplified infinite-plane-wave model supports a same-condition relative comparison but not practical absolute efficiency estimates.
questions.evidence_quote:
considered a simpliﬁed model of a spatially inﬁnite sur-
face under plane-wave illumination, so the model is less
suitable to predict practical absolute numbers as would
be observed in a particular experiment.
